body:
Cans differ between brands, and the numbers printed on a lid do not always tell you how long a can will last or whether it is good value. This guide explains how many pouches are in a typical can, how to work out how long a can lasts for your own use, how to compare cost per pouch and per day, what multi-packs mean for value, how strength and pouch size fit into the maths, what price range to expect at our store, how to avoid buying more than you will use and how to store cans so that they stay fresh. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive. This is general information, not advice to change how much you use.

## Pouch counts
Most cans contain between 15 and 20 pouches, with some holding more. Our catalog lists cans as 15 to 20 pouches per can. The count is printed on the lid and listed in our product descriptions. Some brands sell larger cans, and some sell slimmer ones with more pouches. Always check the count, because two cans at the same price can contain very different numbers.

## How long a can lasts
That depends entirely on how many you use. One pouch a day makes a can of 20 last about three weeks. Five a day makes it last four days. Ten a day makes it last two days. The simple calculation is the number of pouches in the can divided by the number you use each day. Keep your own count for a week, and you will know how many cans you need each month.

### A table in words
- **1 pouch a day:** a 15-pouch can lasts 15 days, a 20-pouch can 20 days.
- **3 pouches a day:** a 15-pouch can lasts 5 days, a 20-pouch can about 6 to 7 days.
- **5 pouches a day:** a 15-pouch can lasts 3 days, a 20-pouch can 4 days.
- **10 pouches a day:** a 15-pouch can lasts 1.5 days, a 20-pouch can 2 days.

## Comparing value
Divide the price by the pouch count to get cost per pouch. A $6 can of 20 is 30 cents each, and a $4 can of 15 is about 27 cents. Include strength when comparing: a higher-strength pouch may be a different product, not just a better deal. Compare like with like, in the same brand and strength, and then compare across brands if you are willing to switch.

## Cost per day
Multiply cost per pouch by how many you use a day. At 30 cents a pouch and five a day, that is $1.50 a day, or about $45 a month. That number is the real comparison with other products, such as vapes. See [pouches vs vapes](/blog/pouches-vs-vapes-key-differences/) and [how to compare vape prices](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). Knowing your daily cost helps you budget.

## Multi-packs
Buying in packs usually reduces cost per can. Our listings include single cans and packs, such as a 5-pack or a 10-pack, and the price updates when you choose the pack size above the Add to Cart button. See [bulk buying](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/). Only buy what you will use before the best-by date. A cheaper can that goes stale is not a bargain.

### A worked example
A single can costs $5.99, and a 5-pack costs $27.99, which is $5.60 a can. Over five cans, you save about $2.00. If you use a can every five days, the 5-pack lasts 25 days, comfortably within a typical date. If you use a can every month, the 5-pack lasts five months, and the later cans may go stale. Match the pack to your use.

## Strength and usage
Stronger pouches may mean fewer per day for the same intake, but nicotine is addictive and this is not advice to change use. See [strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/). If you are comparing two strengths, remember that you may use fewer of the stronger one, and that the cost per day, not per pouch, is the fair measure.

## Pouch size and count
Slim and mini pouches are smaller, so cans may hold more. Standard and large pouches take more space, so cans hold fewer. A larger pouch is not necessarily stronger. When comparing, look at count, strength and size together.

## Price range at our store
Pouch cans in our catalog range from about $4 to $8 per single can, depending on brand and strength, with discounts for packs. Prices are on each product page, and options update the price when you choose them. Orders of $200 or more after discount ship free, and crypto and gift cards save 10%. The minimum order is $100, so many customers buy several cans or packs at once. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/).

## Avoid buying too much
It is tempting to stock up to reach free shipping, but pouches have best-by dates. Estimate how many you use in a month, and buy enough for a month or two. If you share an order with others, split the cans. If you are buying for a shop, see the [wholesale ordering guide](/blog/wholesale-ordering-guide/).

## Storage
Keep cans sealed to preserve freshness; see [storing pouches](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/). Store extras in a cool cupboard, and use the oldest first. Keep them away from children and pets.

## Common mistakes
- **Comparing cans without checking the count.**
- **Buying a large pack that will go stale.**
- **Ignoring strength when comparing price.**
- **Assuming all cans last the same time.**
- **Leaving cans open.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do all cans have the same number of pouches?
No. Check the product page and the lid.

### Is a bigger can better value?
Often, per pouch, but only if you use them in time.

### How can I estimate how many cans I need?
Count how many pouches you use in a week, multiply by four and divide by the pouches in a can.

### Can I return an opened can?
No. Opened items cannot be returned under our policy. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

### Does a pack change the pouch count?
No. A pack contains several cans, each with its own count.

## Shop
Browse [nicotine pouches](/shop/nic-pouches/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A planning worksheet in words
Step one: count how many pouches you use in a typical day. Step two: multiply by thirty for a month. Step three: divide by the number of pouches per can. The result is the number of cans you need each month. Step four: check the cost per can, and multiply to find the monthly cost. Step five: compare packs, and choose the size that you will finish before the best-by date. For example, four pouches a day is 120 a month, which is six cans of 20, or eight cans of 15. At $6 a can, that is $36 to $48 a month.

## Why counts vary
Cans vary because pouches vary in size and because makers choose different pack formats. A slim pouch takes less space than a standard one, so a can can hold more. Some brands deliberately sell smaller cans at lower prices. Always compare the count, not just the can. Our product descriptions list the count, and our specifications show the pack size you choose.

## Keeping track
If you want to keep control of your use, keep a simple tally for a week, on paper or in a note on your phone. Many people find that they use more or fewer pouches than they thought. Knowing the real number helps you plan purchases and spot changes in your habits. If you notice your use rising, consider why, and speak to a healthcare professional if you want support.

## Frequently asked questions about cans and value
### Why does my can seem to have fewer pouches than I expected?
Check the count on the lid and the product page. Cans can differ, and the number is printed on the label.

### Do stronger cans last longer?
A can lasts as long as the number of pouches you use from it. A stronger pouch does not change the count.

### Are there large cans for heavy users?
Some brands offer larger counts. Check the listing. We do not encourage heavier use, and nicotine is addictive.

### How do I avoid running out?
Estimate your monthly use, buy a little over, and keep a spare can sealed in a cool cupboard.

## A reminder about freshness and quantity
Buying slightly more than you need is fine, but buying far more than you will use wastes money, because pouches have best-by dates. Match your purchase to your use, store extras properly and use the oldest first. If you are not sure how much to buy, start with a single can or a small pack, see how long it lasts and then decide. Our product pages show the pack options, and the price updates when you choose.

## Where to read more
See [how to store nicotine pouches](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/) for keeping cans fresh, and [pouch brands compared](/blog/nicotine-pouch-brands-compared/) for choosing between brands.

### A note on counting
If you share cans with another adult, or buy for a household, count each person's use separately, because combined use can make a can vanish faster than you expect. Keep each person's cans labelled, and store them securely, away from children and pets.
